remarks.example:
Use to specify which BlueprintFeatureSelection lists should contain the feature. In the following example the feature is included in as well as any selection referencing CombatFeat e.g. .
FeatureConfigurator.New(CombatFeatName, CombatFeatGuid, FeatureGroup.Feat, FeatureGroup.CombatFeat) .Configure();
remarks.para: If FeatureGroup.TeamworkFeat is specified you should call to make sure it functions correctly with all character features that share teamwork feats.

If you specify FeatureGroups it will automatically set IsClassFeature to true unless you include a group related to race or background:
FeatureGroup.Racial
FeatureGroup.Trait
FeatureGroup.CreatureType
FeatureGroup.AasimarHeritage
FeatureGroup.TieflingHeritage
FeatureGroup.BackgroundSelection
FeatureGroup.DhampirHeritage
FeatureGroup.OreadHeritage
FeatureGroup.KitsuneHeritage
FeatureGroup.HalfOrcHeritage
You can override this by calling .

member.name: M:BlueprintCore.Blueprints.CustomConfigurators.Classes.FeatureConfigurator.AddAsTeamworkFeat(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Populates all the necessary blueprints to make sure the teamwork feat is shared appropriately by various class and archetype abilities.

remarks.para: **IMPORTANT**: This generates blueprints using these GUIDs. That means they are a save dependency just like any other blueprint you create. Once you start using these you cannot stop, or you'll at least need to create dummy blueprints in their place.

If you only set FeatureGroup.TeamworkFeat Monster Tactician, Tactical Leader, Hunter Tactics, Sacred Huntsmaster Tactics, and Battle Prowess are configured automatically. This function is required to update Raging Tactician, Cavalier Tactics, and Vanguard Tactician which all require additional blueprints.
All created blueprints will inherit the name, description, and icon from this feature.

member.name: T:BlueprintCore.Blueprints.CustomConfigurators.RootConfigurator`2
member.summary: Builder API for creating and modifying blueprints.
member.remarks:
Each supported blueprint type has a corresponding Configurator class to create and modify blueprints of that type, e.g. supports BlueprintFeature. Configurators exist for all blueprint types inheriting from , excluding any that are not used in the base game.
Creating a Blueprint
Use New(string, string) to create a blueprint: FeatureConfigurator.New(MyBlueprintName, MyBlueprintGuid)
Once New() is called the blueprint is added to the game library and can be referenced.
Using the Configurator
New() returns a configurator with methods to set or modify blueprint fields and add or modify BlueprintComponents:
FeatureConfigurator.New(MyBlueprintName, MyBlueprintGuid).AddToGroups(FeatureGroup.Feat).AddPrerequisiteAlignment(AlignmentMaskType.LawfulGood).Configure();
Each method call returns the configurator allowing you to chain calls. Nothing is modified on the blueprint until Configure() is called, at which point the changes are applied and validated. Potential problems with the blueprint are logged as warnings.
Modifying an Existing Blueprint
Use For(Blueprint) to modify existing blueprints: CharacterClassConfigurator.For(WizardClassGuid)
Usage is otherwise identical to creating a new blueprint.
For more information see Using BlueprintCore.

remarks.para: This is useful if you want to interact with other content mods without having a dependency. For example you can use this to add a new BlueprintFeature to the appropriate BlueprintFeatureSelection from another mod.

It's recommended to call this after StartGameLoader.LoadPackTOC() by postfixing it. If you use TTT-Core this can be done by implementing IBlueprintCacheInitHandler and calling it in AfterBlueprintCachePatches().

member.name: M:BlueprintCore.Blueprints.CustomConfigurators.RootConfigurator`2.Configure(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Commits the configuration changes to the blueprint.
member.remarks:
After commiting the changes the blueprint is validated and any errors are logged as a warning.
Throws if called twice on the same configurator.

member.name: M:BlueprintCore.Blueprints.CustomConfigurators.RootConfigurator`2.CopyFrom(BlueprintCore.Utils.Blueprint{Kingmaker.Blueprints.BlueprintReference{Kingmaker.Blueprints.BlueprintScriptableObject}},System.Type[])
member.summary: Copies fields and components of the specified types from the blueprint.

remarks.para: NOT A DEEP COPY. This means objects copied are shared between blueprints. Changes to copied objects affect both blueprints.
Recommended when you need to create a nearly identical ability but change some parts such as a ContextRankConfig.

example.code: // Copy the Undead Bloodline's Incorporeal Form ability, replacing the duration w/ Character Level rounds AbilityConfigurator.New(NewIncorporealForm, Guids.NewIncorporealForm) .CopyFrom( AbilityRefs.BloodlineUndeadIncorporealFormAbility, typeof(AbilityEffectRunAction), typeof(AbilityResourceLogic), typeof(SpellComponent)) .AddContextRankConfig(ContextRankConfigs.CharacterLevel()) .Configure();

member.param: Any components in of the listed types are copied. These are shallow copies that are shared by both blueprints.

member.param: Any components in matching the predicate are copied. These are shallow copies that are shared by both blueprints.

remarks.para: Conditions are supported using extension methods. Include the extension namespaces as needed.
When is called the is constructed, validated, and returned. If any errors are detected by they will be logged as a warning.
Do not call twice on the same builder.
If a method calls for a string to represent any type of blueprint, you can pass the blueprint's AssetGuid as a string or as a name you already provided using AddGuidsByName().

item.description: Conditions involving the game map, dungeons, or locations. See also KingdomEx for location related conditions specifically tied to the Kingdom and Crusade system.
Most game mechanics related conditions not included in ContextEx.
Most ContextCondition types. Some ContextCondition types are in more specific extensions such as KingdomEx.
Conditions involving the Kingdom and Crusade system.
Conditions without a better extension container such as game difficulty.
Conditions defined in BlueprintCore and not available in the base game.
Conditions related to the story such as companion stories, quests, name changes, and etudes.

remarks.para: Functions are split into two classes:

item.description: Base class which creates a config with a specific base value type. A context rank config can only have one type so you should only call one of these functions for a config.
Extension class which applies progressions. Like the base value, you can only have a single progression type so you should only call one of these functions for a config.

remarks.para: See ContextRankConfig on the wiki for more details about the component and ContextRankConfig Calculator for help determining which progression to use.
remarks.example:
Create a rank based on modifier with a bonus value of 2 and a max value of 30:
var rankConfig = ContextRankConfigs.StatBonus(StatType.Strength, max: 30).WithBonusValueProgression(2);

Sets the max resulting value.

remarks.para: Only one progression can be applied to a config; only call one of these functions for a config.
If the config should return the base value, no progression is needed.
Integer division is truncated: 3 / 2 = 1 (rounds down) and -3 / 2 = -1 (rounds up).

Config progressions are deceptively named; the functions attempt to name them correctly. For easy mapping to the enum each function comment explains the progression formula and which enums are used. See also the ContextRankConfig Calculator.

types Verifies that is set.

There are some special cases as well, such as .

Note that you can call this method multiple time for a given Validator instance. All of the errors will be bundled into a single error string. This is useful when constructing a several related objects. For example, a single BlueprintConfigurator instance stores a single Validator which is used to validate all of its fields, components, actions, and conditions.
